reviewed.DEBIAN-CVE-2026-73066: AFFECTED, NOT REACHABLE — Tesseract. Heap out-of-bounds WRITE. A crafted .traineddata LSTM component wraps a signed multiplication in Convolve::DeSerialize, undersizing the forward-pass output buffer. Verified present in the vendored 5.5.2 rather than inferred from the CVE's version string: thirdparty/tesseract/src/lstm/convolve.cpp:49 computes `no_ = ni_ * (2 * half_x_ + 1) * (2 * half_y_ + 1)` with no overflow check. SECOND boundary when Stage 6 lands: the attacker input here is the MODEL, not the document. It stays unreachable only while .traineddata is shipped by us and neither the language nor the datadir passed to ocr_init is influenced by a document or by user input.
reviewed.DEBIAN-CVE-2026-73067: AFFECTED, NOT REACHABLE — Tesseract. Heap out-of-bounds READ, crash before image processing. A crafted .traineddata dawg with an unterminated forward-edge run is accepted, after which last_edge walks past edges_. Verified present in the vendored 5.5.2: thirdparty/tesseract/src/dict/dawg.cpp:313-350 checks the magic number and asserts num_edges_ > 0, then reads num_edges_ records and returns true with NO check that the final edge carries the terminator marker; dawg.h:542 then indexes edges_ unchecked. Fixed upstream in 5.5.3. Same reachability and the same model-versus-document boundary as DEBIAN-CVE-2026-73066.

reviewed.DEBIAN-CVE-2025-55780: NOT-APPLICABLE — the EPUB parser is not in the shipped binary. Re-closed on a mechanism after a period UNDER REVIEW, and the history is the useful part. It was NOT-AFFECTED on the premise 'this application opens PDF; no EPUB path is reachable. Revisit if EPUB import is added (Stage 8)'. Measured 2026-08-18, that premise described a guard that did not exist: mz_open calls fz_open_document, which scores every registered handler against the stream's CONTENT as well as the filename, and the shim's 'not a PDF' refusal comes from pdf_specifics AFTER fz_open_document returns — so a file content-scoring as EPUB was opened and parsed by the EPUB handler before being refused. ADR-0016 names the handler set instead of inheriting it. Build-time -DFZ_ENABLE_EPUB=0 removes the registration, and the linker then discarded the unreferenced objects: handlerFootprint.mjs finds no EPUB marker in the rebuilt DLL where it found application/epub+zip and META-INF/container.xml before, and the binary fell from 42,124,800 to 39,373,824 bytes. The parser is absent, so the advisory does not apply to what ships rather than resting on a claim about reachability. Note the discard was PARTIAL across formats — HTML and Office markers survive, and for those the verdict would rest on non-registration rather than absence; this entry is EPUB and EPUB is gone. proof:documenthandlers holds the reachability half end to end.

reviewed.DEBIAN-CVE-2026-40505: NOT-AFFECTED — ANSI escape injection through mutool terminal output. mutool is not shipped (ADR-0010) and no document-derived text reaches a terminal here.
reviewed.DEBIAN-CVE-2026-7233: NOT-AFFECTED — CORRECTED from an earlier AFFECTED verdict that read the CVE text instead of upstream history. The CVE says "up to 1.28.0", which is the report-time upper bound, not a statement that 1.28.0 ships the bug. The fixing commits — Artifex bug 709364 (missing bounds checks in CFF subsetting) and 709365 — landed 2026-05-13, before 1.28.0 shipped 2026-06-26, and are present in .tools/mupdf/1.28.0: subset-cff.c:299 (data_offset > len) and :315 (data_offset + v > len). Verified by executing the trigger against the built engine: scripts/security/cffOobProof.mjs shows a clean throw with the checks and a crash without them. Additionally NOT REACHABLE: font subsetting is opt-in via pdf_subset_fonts, which no code path we ship calls, and pdf_save_document does not reach it.

watch.ARTIFEX-BUG-709567: UNRESOLVED (no CVE, no release) — "potential memory overwrite in CFF2 subsetting", fixed upstream in commit a3caa67262bd on 2026-08-07. In NO released version: it postdates 1.28.2 (2026-08-03) and exists only on master. A memory OVERWRITE, so more serious than the over-read of CVE-2026-7233. NOT REACHABLE here: CFF2 subsetting requires font subsetting, which no shipped code path performs. Take at the first release that contains it, per ADR-0011; until then the register is the record that it is known and waiting.

ocr.why: Tesseract and Leptonica are statically linked into the shipped DLL, and neither is reachable from any of the shim's 24 exported functions (24 in the source, 24 in the built DLL by dumpbin /EXPORTS — the same names). Presence in the binary is NOT the question and does not settle it: ?AVTessErrStream@tesseract@@ is in the 42 MB DLL because MuPDF's own OCR translation units reference it, which says nothing about whether our code can get there. TWO independent measurements settle it, in opposite directions. (1) No shipped file references any of the symbols below, and those symbols are every public MuPDF function with a call path into ocr_init/ocr_recognise/ocr_fin — derived from the compiled source by scripts/security/ocrDoors.mjs, not written by hand, re-derived on every run. (2) Walking the call graph FORWARD from the 24 exports reaches 5583 functions and not one door (scripts/security/shimReach.mjs). The second measurement exists because the first answers a question about our source text rather than about the binary: it would still read clean if an export reached a door through an intermediate that named it for us. mz_save routes through pdf_save_document, never through the writer dispatch. Both walks carry positive controls that must locate something known-present, because a search's failure modes all look like 'found nothing' — which here is the reassuring answer. Leptonica sits behind the same doors because in this build it is armed from exactly one call site, fz_set_leptonica_mem inside ocr_init. Note fz_new_document_writer: it needs no caller to name an OCR symbol at all, because the writer is chosen from a FILE EXTENSION, so a path ending .ocr reaches Tesseract. FZ_ENABLE_OCR_OUTPUT defaults to 1 and libmupdf.vcxproj's Release|x64 configuration defines HAVE_TESSERACT and HAVE_LEPTONICA, so that dispatch is live in the binary we ship — which is why invariant 23 now bans the dispatcher family from shipped code outright, rather than leaving this as a fact to re-establish at every release. This expires when Stage 6 lands OCR, which is the point: the verdict is about this codebase today, not about the engine.

engine-host-containment.why: Invariant 25 requires every document-parsing process to run at the lowest workable integrity level, under a job object bounding memory and process creation, with NO NETWORK, and with no filesystem reach beyond what it was handed. The hosts are not built yet, so this is policy before mechanism, declared here so it cannot decay into a note. The day shipped code names one of the symbols below, this verdict expires and the build fails naming the invariant. WHAT THIS TRIGGER DOES NOT DO: it catches 'a host was created', not 'and it was contained'. It is a prompt to implement, and the thing it prompts is the runtime assertion recorded as a docs/FEATURES.md row — integrity level, job limits and network denial asserted against a RUNNING process, not against the options passed to it. This mechanism is a git grep over path globs (scripts/lib/verdict.mjs), not the C walker that derives the OCR doors, so it reads TypeScript exactly as it reads C — verified against packages/*/src/**. RE-POINTED 2026-08-22 (ruling on WW-2's sibling question). Two clauses of the paragraph above were dead and are corrected in place rather than left standing: electron IS a dependency and apps/desktop/src is no longer a bare index.ts, both false since 2026-08-20. And the trigger itself had gone dead in the way that matters — ADR-0022 moved the hosts to CreateProcessW, so shipped code will NEVER name utilityProcess, and a trigger watching a symbol that cannot appear sits green and reads as coverage. That is the available:true shape at the register level, which is worse than no trigger at all.
engine-host-containment.symbolsWhy: NO witness entry FOR THE THREE ELECTRON SYMBOLS, deliberately — the four Win32 names below do carry one, and that split is the whole of this entry's 2026-08-22 re-pointing. This sentence read 'NO witness entry' flatly until the witnesses landed beside it, which made it a half-true claim of exactly the kind item 7 hunts: the clause about derivation stayed correct and vouched for the blanket that no longer was. The electron three: they are DERIVED from electron.d.ts by the TypeScript compiler (scripts/security/electronSurface.mjs), and a derivation is stronger than a witness — the same reason the OCR doors carry none. The three consequences the old in: null predicted all landed together on 2026-08-20: electron became a dependency, the condition failed, and the list stopped being hand-picked. THE DERIVATION IMMEDIATELY PROVED THE LIST SHORT. It reports the spawn surface by TYPE — every declaration typed as the utility-process factory — and that is utilityProcess AND UtilityProcess. The class was missing from a pair picked by hand, exactly as this verdict's own why warned: a correctly spelt list can still be short. WHY NOT A WITNESS, since one is now possible: the witness shape digests a file, and a digest of a 1.1 MB .d.ts says the file changed rather than that the symbol is still declared in it — finding T-1, which cost a verdict that stayed green with a misspelt symbol. WHY A PARSE AND NOT A SEARCH: electron.d.ts is 56% comments, and on electron@43.4.1 utilityProcess occurs once in prose and MessagePortMain ten times. A text search would witness a symbol that had been REMOVED, which is worse than missing one, and is the reassuring answer. WHAT IT WITNESSES: declarations, and nothing else. Every workflow installs with --ignore-scripts, which fetches electron.d.ts at 1,125,720 bytes and NO BINARY — no dist/, nothing spawnable. Nothing here may be read as evidence that an Electron process can start. MessageChannelMain remains witnessed as a declaration but is NOT part of the derived spawn surface: it is the messaging trigger, picked by hand, and deriving it would need a name pattern rather than a type — a hand-picked rule wearing a derivation's clothes. That limit is stated rather than papered over. RE-POINTED 2026-08-22, AND THE COVERAGE MOVE IS STATED RATHER THAN ABSORBED (audit item 2a, in the WEAKENING direction). The four Win32 names are HAND-PICKED. Nothing derives them: there is no .d.ts for kernel32, and a list of Win32 entry points is not the kind of thing a compiler can enumerate for us. Everything above about derivation being stronger than a witness is still true and now applies to only three of the seven symbols. WHY THIS IS A SMALLER LOSS THAN IT SOUNDS: T-1's rule is that a symbol is derived, witnessed, or printed as unverifiable — and a hand-picked list carrying a witness is stronger than a derived list without one. Each of the four carries a WITNESS pointing at scripts/research/**, where lowboxSpike.mjs names every one of them in working code. That sentence named hostFixture.mjs beside it until 2026-08-22, when WW-1's consolidation folded that file's variant matrix and outcome classifier into the spike and deleted it — two instruments measuring two process types being the finding itself. A typo in this list therefore fails its witness, which is exactly the failure the derivation was bought to prevent. Hand-picking is not the failure mode; an unwitnessed list is. AND THE REGISTER ENFORCED THIS AGAINST ITS OWN AUTHOR: the four names first arrived here carrying reachabilityControl entries instead, which prove a GLOB RESOLVES and say nothing about whether a string could ever match. check:advisories refused all five additions by name. The two mechanisms look alike and do different jobs, and the one that was reached for is the one that reads as coverage. WHY THE ELECTRON SYMBOLS STAY, rather than being replaced: their MEANING changed rather than expiring. They used to mean 'a utility host was written'; they now mean 'ADR-0022 was reverted and somebody went back to the fork route', which is still a thing worth failing the build over. Dropping them would have discarded a live check to fix a dead one.

CreateProcessW.why: T-1 for the first of the four hand-picked names. lowboxSpike.mjs CALLS this function in measured code, so the spelling recorded here is the spelling that ran. The witness scope is a different tree from the one the verdict scans, so a typo cannot satisfy both. UPDATED 2026-08-22: this named hostFixture.mjs beside the spike until WW-1's consolidation deleted that file. All four witnesses now rest on one instrument, which is the point of the consolidation and also a narrower base — a second research file that stops naming a symbol is now the only thing between this witness and a failure.

CreateAppContainerProfile.why: T-1 for the AppContainer half. lowboxSpike.mjs created a real profile with it and deleted it again — executed, not transcribed from documentation.

AssignProcessToJobObject.why: T-1 for the job-object half, invariant 25(b). lowboxSpike.mjs assigns a real job to a real process with it, and after WW-1's consolidation assigns it in some cells and deliberately not in others — the job axis of the variant matrix — so the symbol is exercised on both sides of its own switch. This why said 'three research instruments' until 2026-08-22; one of the three was hostFixture.mjs, which was deleted.

STARTUPINFOEXW.why: T-1 for the extended attribute list, which is how a security capability reaches CreateProcessW at all. Listed as a symbol in its own right because a factory could plausibly avoid naming CreateAppContainerProfile — by reusing a profile created earlier — and still cannot avoid this struct.

engine-host-factory-wired.why: THE PATH KEY, beside engine-host-containment's SYMBOL key, because the two have different silent failures and neither covers the other. A symbol set is evaded by reaching Win32 through a wrapper or under a different name; a path key is evaded by putting the factory somewhere nobody is watching. This one fires when the ENGINE HOST FACTORY IS WIRED INTO MAIN, whatever it chooses to call the Win32 functions it uses. The trigger is classifyContainment — ADR-0023 section 5's startup check, which lives in packages/kernel and which the factory must call, because the factory is the side that can kill the process and the kernel is the side that may not name Electron. A factory that creates a contained host without consulting it is a host nobody verified, which is the one shape invariant 25 cannot tolerate. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, said plainly: it catches 'the factory was wired', not 'and the host it makes is contained'. Same prompt-to-implement status as its sibling, and the same docs/FEATURES.md row is what discharges it. SCOPED TO apps/*/src/** deliberately: classifyContainment is defined and tested under packages/kernel/src/**, so scanning that glob would fire on the day it was written rather than on the day it was used.
engine-host-factory-wired.symbolsWhy: One symbol, hand-picked, and witnessed the same way the Win32 four are. WHY NOT THE FACTORY'S OWN MODULE PATH, which was the first idea: a glob matching no files is indistinguishable from a glob that is wrong, and the pre-state of this trigger is precisely 'that directory does not exist yet' — so the witness and the subject would have been the same absence. Keying on a symbol that DOES exist somewhere is what makes the walk's silence checkable.

classifyContainment.why: Defined in packages/kernel/src/host/containment.ts, exported from the package index and exercised by containment.test.ts. The verdict scans apps/*/src/**; this scans where the symbol lives, so 'no references' over there means the factory is unwired rather than that the walk is blind.

renderer-facing-errors-carry-no-text.why: THE SUCCESSOR TO kernel-error-path-sanitisation, which EXPIRED as designed on 2026-08-19 when the first handler named DocumentService from apps/desktop/src. That verdict rested on 'no IPC handler calls DocumentService yet', and the handler is now written; re-arming the old input would be a verdict resting on a fact that is no longer true. Recorded here rather than deleted, because the old one was a prompt to implement and this one is what the implementation now claims. THE CLAIM: no filesystem path reaches the renderer through an IPC failure. THE BASIS, which is a TYPE rather than a filter: a wire Failure is a code, plus an incident id when a diagnostic was withheld, and nothing else — no message, no stack, no cause, and failureSchema is two disjoint .strict() shapes so an extra field is rejected rather than ignored. A field that does not exist cannot leak, which is why this is not a sanitiser that has to be right on every message ever written (B5). THE INPUT ITS TRUTH RESTS ON: no code under apps/*/src/** builds a diagnostic. toStructuredError copies message, copies stack and RECURSES INTO cause with itself; structuredErrorSchema is the wire shape of that diagnostic. Either one named from a handler is somebody assembling free text on the renderer-facing side, and that is the only remaining route by which a path could cross — a handler cannot put text in a Failure, but it could put one in a channel's RESULT if a result schema ever carried a diagnostic. WHAT THIS TRIGGER DOES NOT DO: it catches 'a handler reached for the diagnostic type', not 'and the diagnostic leaked'. It is a prompt to re-read ADR-0009 §9 before writing that line, and the evidence that the claim holds today lives in apps/desktop/src/documentCommands.test.ts — the renderer-facing failure carries the path in no field, with a control asserting the path IS in message, stack and a NESTED cause main-side, mutation-tested in the direction that matters: removing the path from the fixture reddens the control alone. Scoped to apps/*/src/** because packages/shared and packages/contract define these symbols and must name them.

toStructuredError.why: Defined in result.ts and named by incident.ts. The verdict scans apps/*/src/** — disjoint scopes, so the witness cannot be satisfied by the very reference whose appearance would expire the verdict.

structuredErrorSchema.why: Defined in schemas.ts and re-exported by the contract index. Same disjointness as above.

pdf_subset_fonts.why: Font subsetting is opt-in in MuPDF. fz_subset_cff_for_gids is reached only through pdf_subset_fonts, which pdf_save_document does not call and no shipped path invokes. This is what makes both verdicts NOT REACHABLE — and it is a claim about THIS codebase, not about the engine. Optimise and export are exactly the features that will call it, and 709567 is a memory OVERWRITE that no release fixes, so enabling subsetting inherits a live one.

ADR-0015 and ADR-0017 name the symbol as part of the decisions that rest on it. Deliberately NOT the register or the script that reads it: witnessing a symbol in the file that declares it is circular, since a misspelling would be present in both places and find itself. The ADRs are independent text, and their losing the name would itself be worth stopping on.

reachabilityControl.why: Every verdict above is a SEARCH, and a search reports 'no references' for every way it can be broken — a glob matching no files, a symbol misspelt here, git grep run from the wrong root. All of them look exactly like the answer everyone hoped for. So the walk must first find something it is known to find, per path glob, on every run (audit item 4b). This symbol is the shim's single registration call site (ADR-0016, invariant 23): it is present by construction and its disappearance would itself be worth stopping on.

The control proving packages/*/src/** resolves. A control over native/** says nothing about whether this glob matches any files, and pdf_subset_fonts and engine-host-containment both rest on it being scanned. CapabilityRegistry is the oldest class in packages/kernel and is named by its own module, its test and the kernel index.

The control proving the single-file glob used by kernel-holds-canonical-bytes resolves. A glob naming one file is the easiest kind to get wrong — a rename, a move, a typo — and every one of those failures reports 'no references', which is that verdict's passing answer. checkWriteTarget is defined in that file and named by its own doc comment.

The control proving apps/*/src/** resolves, and the one that matters most: renderer-facing-errors-carry-no-text scans ONLY this glob, so a glob that matched nothing would leave that verdict permanently, silently green. 'export' is deliberately a weak symbol and exactly the right control, because what is being controlled for is whether any file under this glob is read at all — it held when apps/desktop/src was a bare 'export {};' and it holds now that the composition point and the first handler live there. A SECOND PROPERTY OF THIS GLOB, learned by running it: scripts/lib/verdict.mjs resolves an absent-symbol input with `git grep`, which reads TRACKED files only. A newly written, still-untracked source file is therefore invisible to every reachability verdict — so an author writing the first handler sees green until the moment they stage it. That is not a defect in the tracked-only choice, which exists so build artefacts and vendored trees do not fire every verdict constantly; it is a consequence nobody had written down, and it is exactly the window in which the work is being done.
